eips.title: LUCID Key Publisher Priority Lists
eips.summary: Jannik's newly numbered EIP factoring optionality out of Lucid into a standalone proposal was presented and discussed for next steps.

moments.context: Justin confirmed the EIP received its number, 8491, and Loring noted it was less memorable than the placeholder EIPXXXX.
Justin asked if folks had read the EIP and posted a link in chat, explaining the decision to isolate the optionality problem into a separate EIP from Lucid.
Jannik presented EIP 8491, noting it is technically the same proposal as before—validator voting contract and priority list enforcement—now formatted as a standalone EIP with added rationale.
Mercy offered to add the new EIP's changes (commitments, signature fields, validity check) to the CL spec as a separate addition, and Justin agreed as long as they stay separate.

eips.title: LUCID encrypted mempool
eips.summary: The base encrypted mempool proposal: long and complex enough that the optionality problem was split out into a separate EIP, but otherwise stable and ready to prototype.

moments.context: Justin Florentine said the group decided to isolate the optionality problem in a subsequent EIP rather than fold it into Lucid.
He described the Lucid EIP as quite long and fairly complicated, with a lot of different concepts; it mentions and tries to describe the optionality problem, which is not quite quantified yet.
Justin noted Lucid itself hasn't really changed all that much, arguing the major decisions were settled enough to start prototyping.
Jannik said which document is easier to read depends on familiarity with Lucid: those already familiar should find the new standalone EIP easier.
Justin said they should fully expect to discover and throw out aspects of Lucid and the new optionality stuff after it makes first contact with a devnet.
